name: tmatmul16
summary: C[t] = A[t] B[t] for TILES independent 16x16x16 tiles, f16-grid f32 inputs, f32 accumulate
provenance: authored for OpenAccel Lab (Apache-2.0); the shape follows the tile kernels of aien-dev/omega-mv PR #869 (unmerged, head 6d08fd9c, seed/kflow/specs/tmatmul16.spec and seed/kflow/sm121/tmatmul16.s2)

c.why: Inputs are k*2^-10 with |k|<=1024, so every value is exact in f16 and in f32, every product a*b is an integer multiple of 2^-20 with |a*b|<=1 and is exact in f32, and with or without FMA a length-16 dot product starting from 0 takes at most 15 rounded additions (the first product enters exactly). Higham Thm 3.1/3.5 for any summation order with round-to-nearest (u=2^-24): |d-ref| <= gamma(15)*sum_k |a_ik b_kj|; reference.py passes that sum as scale. WolframLanguageEvaluator: u=2^-24; gam[n_]:=n u/(1-n u); N[gam[15],12] -> 8.94070470992e-7 (PR #869 quotes gamma_15 = 1.78814254071e-6 with u=2^-23 to allow any rounding mode; every entrant here rounds to nearest, so u=2^-24). On this grid the bound is not the binding fact: every partial sum is an integer multiple of 2^-20 of magnitude <= 16*2^20 = 2^24 (WolframLanguageEvaluator: 16*1024*1024==2^24 -> True), hence exact in f32, so a correct entrant's observed error is 0; the bound is what the contract guarantees for general f16 tiles. One dropped k term changes an element by |a_ik b_kj| up to 1, far above the bound, so gemm_offbyone fails.
